newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Jardine says no plans to change listing position.
newsitem.headline: Jardine says no plans to change listing position.

text.p: The Hong Kong-based Jardine Group has no plans to change its share listing position, Neil M. McNamara, company secretary of Jardine Matheson Ltd, said on Friday.
"We have no plans to change the position of our listing," McNamara told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He was responding to stock market rumours that the Jardine group of companies would be relisting in Hong Kong post the 1997 handover.
Shares of HongKong Land Holdings, Jardine Matheson, Jardine Strategic continued to rise for the second consecutive day in active trading on Friday morning.
The Jardine Group has its primary listing in London, but most of its shares are traded in Singapore.
At 0250 GMT, HongKong Land topped the Singapore actives list with more than 4.5 million shares changing hands and was up seven cents to US$2.80.

Jardine Matheson and Jardine Stratigic were also active and both touched new 1997 highs of US$7.80 and US$3.90 respectively. "All the Jardine group shares and also the warrants are moving. There are renewed rumours of the group might relist in Hong Kong soon," said a broker with a Singapore firm.

However another institutional dealer said the Jardine group was just getting attention as the handover approaches. "Hong Kong stocks are hot and the Jardine group is rising like the rest of the Hong Kong market."

Brokers said another reason for the rise was the overnight news the London branch of Deutsche Bank AG said it expected to issue call warrants on a basket of companies which included HongKong Land and Jardine Matheson.
